title: Facial Recognition & Biometric Privacy Hardening Checklist
metaDescription: Protect yourself from facial recognition surveillance and biometric data collection with this comprehensive privacy hardening checklist.
intro: Facial recognition technology is now widespread in public spaces, retail stores, and online platforms. This checklist helps you protect your biometric data from unconsented collection and reduce your exposure to facial recognition surveillance systems.

items.task: Opt out of Clearview AI's facial recognition database
items.why: Clearview AI has scraped billions of photos from social media and websites to build facial recognition profiles without consent.
items.howTo: Visit Clearview AI's opt-out page, submit your photo and personal information to request removal. Note that this process requires providing the data you want removed.

items.task: Review and limit publicly visible photos on social media
items.why: Public photos are scraped by facial recognition companies to build databases and train AI systems.
items.howTo: Set Facebook, Instagram, and Twitter profiles to private. Review photo tagging settings and disable automatic face tagging. Remove or limit visibility of photos showing your face clearly.

items.task: Disable automatic face recognition on social platforms
items.why: Social media platforms use facial recognition to automatically identify and tag you in photos, creating searchable biometric profiles.
items.howTo: On Facebook: Settings > Privacy > Face Recognition > No. On Google Photos: disable face grouping. On iPhone: Settings > Photos > disable 'People & Places'.

items.task: Use privacy-focused browsers for sensitive browsing
items.why: Standard browsers can expose your browsing patterns to sites that collect biometric data or track facial recognition opt-out requests.
items.howTo: Use a privacy-focused browser or Tor Browser when researching facial recognition topics, submitting opt-out requests, or accessing privacy tools to prevent tracking.

items.task: Regularly search for your images online
items.why: Monitor if your photos appear on websites that might be scraped by facial recognition companies.
items.howTo: Use reverse image search tools like Google Images, TinEye, or Yandex. Upload recent photos of yourself and check where they appear online. Request removal from unauthorized sites.

items.task: Minimize uploading clear facial photos online
items.why: Every photo you post online can potentially be scraped and added to facial recognition databases.
items.howTo: When posting photos, use angles that obscure your face, wear sunglasses or masks, or use photo editing to blur facial features. Consider using cartoon avatars instead of real photos.

items.why: Physical disguises can reduce the accuracy of facial recognition systems in public spaces and retail locations.
items.howTo: Wear wide-brimmed hats, oversized sunglasses, or face masks in surveilled areas. Consider anti-surveillance clothing with patterns designed to confuse AI systems. Scarves and hoodies also provide face coverage.

items.task: Identify facial recognition locations in your area
items.why: Knowing which stores, venues, and public spaces use facial recognition helps you make informed decisions about where to go.
items.howTo: Check local news reports, privacy advocacy websites, and store privacy policies. Some retailers like Walmart and certain stadiums openly use facial recognition. Plan alternative routes and shopping locations.

items.task: Use cash for purchases in surveilled locations
items.why: Facial recognition combined with payment data creates detailed profiles of your movements and purchasing habits.
items.howTo: Pay with cash at stores that use facial recognition. If using cards, consider using different cards or prepaid cards to reduce data correlation between facial recognition and purchases.

items.why: Enrolling in facial recognition systems for convenience gives companies permanent biometric templates that can be shared or breached.
items.howTo: Decline facial recognition unlock features at stores, airports, or venues. Use alternative authentication methods like PIN codes, passwords, or traditional ID checks instead of biometric options.

items.why: Apps can use your phone's camera for facial recognition without your knowledge, even when you're not actively using camera features.
items.howTo: Review app permissions and revoke camera access for unnecessary apps. Use camera covers or cases with camera blocks. Keep phones in bags or face-down in sensitive locations.

items.task: Take extra precautions at protests and gatherings
items.why: Law enforcement and private companies often use facial recognition at protests, which can lead to identification and potential retaliation.
items.howTo: Wear masks, bandanas, or other face coverings. Use matte makeup or face paint to disrupt facial recognition algorithms. Leave phones at home or in airplane mode with cameras covered.

items.task: Research facial recognition laws in your area
items.why: Understanding your legal rights helps you know when facial recognition use is illegal and what recourse you have.
items.howTo: Check if your city or state has banned facial recognition use by police or businesses. Cities like San Francisco and Boston have restrictions. Research your rights under GDPR, CCPA, or local privacy laws.

items.why: Reporting violations helps enforce existing laws and builds evidence for stronger regulations.
items.howTo: File complaints with local authorities, privacy regulators, or consumer protection agencies when you encounter unlawful facial recognition use. Document evidence with photos or videos when safe to do so.

items.why: Collective advocacy is essential for creating stronger laws that protect biometric privacy rights.
items.howTo: Contact elected representatives about facial recognition concerns. Support organizations like EFF, ACLU, or local privacy advocacy groups. Stay informed about legislation and participate in public comment periods.

items.task: Ask businesses about their facial recognition policies
items.why: Public pressure and awareness can encourage businesses to adopt more privacy-friendly practices.
items.howTo: Ask store managers or customer service about facial recognition use. Request written policies. Choose to shop at businesses that don't use facial recognition when possible.

items.task: Keep records of facial recognition encounters
items.why: Documentation helps if you need to file complaints, participate in class action lawsuits, or report privacy violations.
items.howTo: Note dates, locations, and circumstances when you encounter facial recognition systems. Save screenshots of privacy policies and opt-out confirmations. Keep receipts from requests for data deletion.

pro_tips: Infrared LEDs embedded in hats or glasses can overwhelm facial recognition cameras, but may not be legal in all jurisdictions and can draw unwanted attention.
Face makeup techniques using geometric patterns or contrasting colors can confuse facial recognition algorithms while still looking stylish.
Check your state's biometric privacy laws - Illinois, Texas, and Washington have strong protections that give you legal recourse against unauthorized facial recognition use.
Consider using privacy-focused alternatives like a privacy-focused browser when researching facial recognition topics to prevent your searches from being tracked and correlated.
Some facial recognition systems can still identify you through gait analysis and body shape, so varying your walking style and clothing silhouette adds extra protection.
